title.narrative: Dignified and Inclusive Multi-Sectoral Response for IDPs in Harbu Jara Site, North Wollo Zone through Cash, Protection, WASH, and Shelter Support

description.narrative: ltpgtUnion of Ethiopian Women and Children Associations (UEWCA) proposes a nine-month integrated multi-sectoral emergency response project targeting conflict-affected internally displaced persons (IDPs) residing in the Jara IDP site, Habru Woreda, North Wollo Zone, Amhara Region. The project aims to deliver a dignified and inclusive humanitarian response through coordinated interventions in Protection (including GBV), WASH, Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items (ES/NFI), and Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPC). With a total budget of USD 720000, the project will reach 8,626 IDPs, prioritizing women, girls, and persons with disabilities who face heightened risks of violence, exclusion, and neglect.ltbrgtThe humanitarian situation in the Jara IDP site remains critical, with displaced households struggling due to limited access to safe water, sanitation facilities, protection services, and adequate shelter. Overcrowding, inadequate lighting, and poor hygiene conditions continue to increase the risk of communicable diseases and worsen exposure to gender-based violence.ltbrgtThe ES/NFI needs in Jara are extremely high and far exceed current response capacity. Communal shelter infrastructure is deteriorating rapidly, leaving thousands exposed to the elements. Of the originally installed six-unit communal hangars, half are out of use due to structural collapse and disrepair. The remaining units, though still standing, have sustained significant damage to roofing, frames, and flooring, reducing their safety and functionality. Many families are forced to live in overcrowded, unsafe sections or makeshift extensions made from torn plastic sheets. This situation has intensified protection risks, contributed to rising health concerns, and left the most vulnerable—especially women-headed households, older persons, and persons with disabilities—without dignified living conditions. The gap in shelter rehabilitation and household items is therefore severe and requires urgent intervention.ltbrgtUnder the Protection/GBV component, UEWCA will provide survivor-centered GBV response services including case management, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and distribution of dignity kits. Awareness sessions will engage men, women, and youth to challenge harmful norms, reduce GBV risks, and strengthen community-based protection systems. UEWCA will also reinforce safe and confidential referral pathways to ensure timely access to health, psychosocial, and legal services for survivors.ltbrgtThe WASH component will rehabilitate and solarize non-functional water schemes to restore sustainable access to safe water. The intervention includes hygiene promotion, distribution of hygiene kits and water treatment chemicals, and construction of gender-sensitive and disability-inclusive latrines and bathing facilities to improve privacy, dignity, and safety.ltbrgtThe ES/NFI and Shelter component will address the critical shelter gap by providing emergency shelter repair kits, essential household items such as blankets, sleeping mats, kitchen sets, and solar lamps, and offering technical support to highly vulnerable households. Priority will be given to women-headed families, persons with disabilities, and older persons to ensure equitable access.ltbrgtMulti-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPC) will enhance flexibility and dignity for IDPs, enabling households to meet urgent needs such as food, health services, and household supplies. Cash support will reduce negative coping mechanisms and stimulate local markets, contributing to early recovery and self-reliance.ltbrgtCross-cutting issues, including gender equality, disability inclusion, accountability to affected populations (AAP), environmental considerations, and localization—will be integrated throughout project implementation. UEWCA will ensure that women, youth, and persons with disabilities are meaningfully engaged in planning, implementation, and monitoring through inclusive consultations and accessible feedback mechanismsltbrgtlt/pgt
